The annual law that authorizes funding levels and sets policy for the Defense Department and the nuclear weapons programs of the Energy Department. It has been enacted every year for more than six decades, which makes it the most reliable vehicle in Congress for national security legislation of all kinds.

## Key provisions

- Authorizes appropriations for procurement, research, operations, personnel, and military construction; actual funding comes from separate appropriations acts.
- Sets personnel policy, including pay, end strength, and military justice.
- Creates, extends, and limits security cooperation and counterterrorism authorities.
- Routinely carries unrelated or loosely related titles, such as the intelligence and State Department authorizations and sanctions measures.

## Why it matters

Much of this wiki passed through it. It carried the [Global Magnitsky Act](glomag-2016.qmd), the [Caesar Act](caesar-2019.qmd), the [Export Control Reform Act](ecra-2018.qmd), [FIRRMA](firrma-2018.qmd), [Chapter 16 of Title 10](seccoop-2016.qmd), and the [Nunn-Cohen Amendment](nunn-cohen-1986.qmd), and the FY2026 act repealed the [2002 Iraq AUMF](aumf-iraq-2002.qmd) and the [1991 Gulf War AUMF](aumf-gulf-1991.qmd). Knowing which year's act did what is often the fastest way to trace a provision.

## Current status

The most recent enacted act is for fiscal year 2026 (Pub. L. 119-60, signed December 18, 2025). For fiscal year 2027 the House passed H.R. 8800 on July 22, 2026; the Senate bill (S. 4784) had not passed, and final action was expected in the post-election session. Check current status.

[Last checked November 10, 2026.]{.checked}

## Where it sits

- **Layer.** Specific authorization. Laws aimed at a particular conflict, country, program, or problem. Most work through a framework statute: an AUMF through the War Powers Resolution, a sanctions act through IEEPA. ([How the layers work](../study/index.qmd#the-authority-stack))
- **Builds on.** [Case-Zablocki Act](case-zablocki-1972.qmd), [Insurrection Act](insurrection-1807.qmd), [Posse Comitatus Act](posse-comitatus-1878.qmd), [Military Commissions Act](mil-commissions-2006.qmd), [Nunn-Lugar Act](nunn-lugar-1991.qmd), [Defense Production Act](dpa-1950.qmd), [Smith-Mundt Act](smith-mundt-1948.qmd), [UCMJ](ucmj-1950.qmd), [Section 2808 (construction)](sec2808-milcon-1982.qmd), [Title 10 U.S.C.](title10-usc.qmd).
- **Built upon by.** [Detainee Treatment Act](dta-2005.qmd), [Nunn-Cohen Amendment](nunn-cohen-1986.qmd), [Global Magnitsky Act](glomag-2016.qmd), [Caesar Act](caesar-2019.qmd), [Export Control Reform Act](ecra-2018.qmd), [FIRRMA (CFIUS)](firrma-2018.qmd), [Security Cooperation (Ch. 16)](seccoop-2016.qmd), [Section 127e](sec127e-2004.qmd), [Section 394 (cyber)](sec394-cyber-2018.qmd), [Section 284 (counterdrug)](sec284-counterdrug-1990.qmd), [Civilian Casualty Report](civcas-report-2017.qmd), [Civilian Casualty Policy](civcas-policy-2018.qmd), [Ex Gratia Payments](ex-gratia-2019.qmd), [Civilian Protection Center](cp-coe-2022.qmd), [Ukraine Security Assistance Initiative](usai-2016.qmd).
- **Codified in.** [Title 10 U.S.C.](title10-usc.qmd), [Title 50 U.S.C.](title50-usc.qmd).
- **Era.** Building the national security state ([timeline](../study/timeline.qmd)).
- **Study.** [Unit 4: The power of the purse](../study/units/purse.qmd) (further reading); [Unit 8: Organizing and commanding the military](../study/units/defense-organization.qmd) (core reading).
- **Who's involved.** [HASC](../whos-who.qmd#hasc), [SASC](../whos-who.qmd#sasc), [DoD](../whos-who.qmd#dod).
